observation: Frozen ZN-E010: split 2021 MAPE 0.3325, Acc@15 0.3665, RMSE 425.0; long-life underprediction on every run. ZN-E015 (statistical stat_tail_balance) did not lift long-life cells: the tail term keeps the 1/y scaling. KDE rarity weighting (alpha 0.5) on the 2021 train cells gives w(1235)=1.26 vs w(190)=0.92 (only 1.37x), so it is not evidence-led either. Zn-ion physics check on the 59 train cells with >= 100 cycles: Spearman(relative discharge-capacity fade phi_10->100, log EOL) = -0.957; 32/59 cells show break-in (phi < 0); domain P90 phi = 0.15. Frozen ZN-E010 held-out violation rates: P0 0.150, P0c 0.149, P4b 0.303, P2 0.226 (alpha = alpha_max).
primary_hypothesis: The label-free physics rule 'a uniformly faster-fading battery cannot live longer' (P0, loss.md §4.6), which holds strongly on ZN-coin (Spearman -0.957), lowers the held-out what-if violation rate by >= 50% vs ZN-E010 without hurting accuracy, and by teaching a fade-to-life ordering helps separate slow-fading long-life cells: KEEP under §7 vs ZN-E010.
question_inherited: Does a label-free Zn-ion fade-monotonicity physics loss improve ZN-E010's accuracy and physical consistency?
unresolved_from_reference: Whether ZN-E010 violates the fade-to-life ordering and whether enforcing it helps the long-life tail.
why_this_experiment: loss.md §4.6 mandatory physics order P0 -> P4 -> P0c -> P2 (P4 is unsafe here: 32/59 train cells rise, the R4-E064 failure mode; P4b is the safe variant later). P0 is label-free, in standardized units (no 1/y factor), and its rule is strongly supported by ZN-coin train data. Statistical alternatives are weak (tail term 1.19x, rarity 1.37x).
modification: Loss only: L = RelativeHuber_0.15 + lambda * L_P0, L_P0 = mean ReLU(f(x~) - sg[f(x)]), x~ = discharge-capacity channel scaled by (1 - alpha r_n) on observed cycles, r_n = clip((n-10)/90,0,1), alpha ~ U(0, alpha_max(d)), alpha_max = P90 train fade (0.15; dedicated RNG seed+10000). lambda = rho * median ||grad L_main|| / ||grad L_cal|| on 3 fixed train batches with the unsigned calibration loss (loss.md §5.2), rho = 0.5.
changed_components: Objective: added label-free physics term P0 (uniform-fade what-if), lambda calibrated from gradients.
held_constant_components: Frozen ZN-E010 architecture (98,113 params, GELU, anchored fade encoder), Relative Huber delta 0.15 main loss, Adam lr 5e-4, batch 128, seed 2021, split 2021, A2-ZN epochs, checkpoint rule, data.
controlled_variables: Training seed 2021, split 2021, minimum 5 / maximum 100 epochs, patience 5 after epoch 5, diagnostics every 50 steps; lambda2 never tuned on validation.
expected_evidence: MAPE/Acc@15/RMSE/DB-MAPE vs ZN-E010; held-out P0 violation rate (alpha in {0.25,0.5,1.0} x alpha_max) for ZN-E016 and ZN-E010; lambda, R, cosine, active fraction (summary.loss_balance); EOL-band bias; gradient gate.
rejection_condition: Primary rule (program.md §7, vs frozen reference ZN-E010 MAPE 0.3325 / RMSE 425.0 / Acc@15 0.3665 / DB-MAPE 0.3325). KEEP iff [A: MAPE <= 0.3245 AND RMSE <= 435.0] OR [B: RMSE <= 404.0 AND MAPE <= 0.3355] OR [C: Acc@15 >= 0.3865 AND MAPE <= 0.3355 AND RMSE <= 435.0], AND Acc@15 >= 0.3365 (A/B) AND DB-MAPE <= 0.3425 AND gradient gate PASS AND loss balance PASS or SATISFIED (loss.md §5.3; BALANCE_FAIL -> DISCARD) AND prediction SD >= 10% of target SD; otherwise DISCARD. Physics claim only if the held-out violation rate falls vs ZN-E010 and accuracy does not get worse (loss.md §4.6).
minimum_evidence_requirements: At least five complete epochs; finite MAPE, Acc@15, MAE, and RMSE from one checkpoint; sample and unique-cell counts for every domain; gradient, update, activation, prediction, mask, and compute diagnostics.
required_diagnostics: Epoch learning curve; selected and minimum-MAPE epochs; cycle_stem, residual_blocks, fade_encoder, inter_summary and head gradients and updates; activation health; prediction spread and bias; prefix, domain and EOL errors; padding sensitivity; parameters, memory, time, throughput. Loss balance: lambda2, R_j median, cosine, active fraction (loss.md §5.3).
